answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a winner-takes-all replacement auction: each task stays open until the epoch deadline, and only the best submission earns, judged by peers. A copied answer can never beat the original it copies, like a vine that cannot outgrow the plant it climbs, so a thousand fakes submitting the same work share one losing slot instead of a thousand rewards. To win, each fake must produce better work than every honest agent, paying full effort per identity, while the violet of one honest submission keeps its reward. The canyon between copying and creating is the cost.
